sense: the skilled way a task is done

terms.gloss: skill, technique; the rules of an art
evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.157: ars disserendī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Skill and the body of rules that teaches it, often with a gerund in the genitive: ars dīcendī, the technique of speaking. It is also the craft itself (see skill, trade).
The skill shown in a piece of work; also a craft or trade, and a theory or system (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: a method, a way of doing something
terms.comment: For technique as a method or procedure rather than a skill: ratiō + gerund (see approach).

phrases.latin: simulācrum Diānae singulārī opere artificiōque perfectum
phrases.english: a statue of Diana finished with singular workmanship and technique

sources: Lewis & Short: ars · Lewis & Short: artificium · Lewis & Short: ratio
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 298.
